reading.body:
Julie Fedorchak's AI record holds 16 dated events: two AI bill cosponsorships, four recorded votes, and ten contributions from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta political committees.

The money is the densest part of the record. Ten contributions arrive between June 2025 and August 2026, from four companies' PACs, in amounts of $1,000 to $5,000. One entry is a negative $2,000 from Google on 2025-07-31, which reverses an identical $2,000 from the day before. The contributions cluster in the months around the recorded votes, but the data does not establish that any contribution preceded, followed, or influenced any vote.

The legislative side is thin. Two cosponsorships, the TAKE IT DOWN Act in January 2025 and the Small AI Innovators Empowerment Act in March 2026, plus four yea votes on bills the data does not name beyond their numbers. Nothing here shows what any of those bills would do to data centers, interconnection queues, or power procurement, which is where AI scaling actually binds.

What the record does not cover matters as much as what it does. It holds no committee assignments, no floor statements, no letters to agencies, and no positions on grid or siting policy. A reader can see which AI-adjacent committees gave money and which AI bills drew a vote. A reader cannot see what Fedorchak has done about the electricity and buildings that AI depends on, because this data does not contain it.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Julie Fedorchak: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 16 events.
